- **Time Complexity**: Depends on the quadtree depth.
In the worst case (uniform grid), it is $O(N)$ where $N$ is the number of cells.
Adaptive splitting reduces this for smooth regions.
- **Memory Complexity**: $O(N)$ for vertices and indices.
Quadtree overhead adds a constant factor.
- **When to use**: When smooth surfaces are preferred and sharp features are not critical.
- **When not to use**: When sharp features must be preserved or when edge-based precision is required.
